prompt:
Rewrite the following so it is easier to read. Keep every fact and number.

This retry loop hammers the payment gateway the way a toddler hammers an elevator button. Five attempts at a fixed 200 ms interval means a 2-second outage burns the whole budget before the upstream even recovers, and every client, synchronized by the same deploy, stampedes back in lockstep: a thundering-herd-on-a-timer. Swap in exponential backoff with full jitter (base 100 ms, cap 10 s, per the AWS architecture guidance) and wrap the call in a circuit breaker. The catch block, which currently swallows every exception including 400-series validation errors, should retry only on 429, 503, and connection resets; a malformed request will fail identically on attempt five. Also, the idempotency key header retry logic needs a test: I suspect duplicate charges slip through when the first POST times out but succeeds server-side. Please ticket the metrics gap too.
text:
This retry loop hammers the payment gateway like a toddler pressing an elevator button. It makes five attempts at a fixed 200 ms interval, so a 2-second outage uses up the whole retry budget before the upstream recovers. Every client was started by the same deploy, so they all retry at the same moments and flood the gateway together (a thundering herd on a timer).

Please make these changes:

1. **Backoff:** Switch to exponential backoff with full jitter (base 100 ms, cap 10 s, per the AWS architecture guidance), and wrap the call in a circuit breaker.
2. **Catch block:** It currently swallows every exception, including 400-series validation errors. It should retry only on 429, 503, and connection resets, because a malformed request will fail the same way on attempt five.
3. **Idempotency test:** Add a test for the idempotency key header retry logic. I suspect duplicate charges slip through when the first POST times out but succeeds on the server.
4. **Metrics:** Please open a ticket for the metrics gap too.
